intro: Searching for an annuity advisor near you usually means you have a pension pot and want to turn part of it into a regular income that lasts, and you would rather talk it through with someone face to face or close to home. An annuity is a long-term decision, so it is worth understanding your options before you commit. iComply can introduce you to a pension adviser who deals with annuities and quotes you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for an annuity advisor usually need
need_lead: Most people behind this search are weighing up whether an annuity suits them and want local, regulated advice before deciding.
needs: You have a defined contribution pension pot and are thinking about buying an annuity to give you a regular income for life.
You have health conditions or a lifestyle that might qualify you for an enhanced annuity, and you want an adviser to explore that properly.
You are unsure whether to take an annuity now or later, and you want to understand how inflation protection and other options affect the income you would get.
You have been offered an annuity by your existing pension provider and want to know whether shopping around could give you a better rate.
You would prefer to sit down with an adviser near you rather than handle the decision alone online.
context_heading: Shopping around and checking who is authorised
context: Annuity rates vary between providers, so comparing quotes across the market is a normal part of getting an annuity, and an adviser can do that for you. Your health and lifestyle can affect the rate you are offered, which is why enhanced annuities exist for people with certain conditions.

Financial advice in the UK is regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Check that any adviser or firm is authorised, or is an appointed representative of an authorised firm, on the FCA register. If something goes wrong you can complain to the firm, then to the Financial Ombudsman Service, and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme may protect you if an authorised firm fails.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Say roughly how your pension is held, such as a defined contribution pot from a workplace or personal pension.
Mention whether you have any health conditions or a lifestyle that might make an enhanced annuity relevant.
Explain whether you have already had a quote from your current provider and whether you are comparing it.
Say whether inflation protection matters to you, and whether you want income to continue for a spouse or partner.
Describe whether you want advice on the whole pot or only part of it, and whether you have other pensions to consider.
Let us know your location so we can introduce you to a pension adviser near you.
questions: Are you authorised by the FCA to advise on annuities, and can you show me your entry on the FCA register?
Will you compare annuity quotes across the whole market rather than only my current provider?
Could my health or lifestyle mean I qualify for an enhanced annuity, and how would you assess that?
How would inflation protection affect the income I receive, and is it worth considering for my situation?
What happens to the income if I die, and can it continue for my spouse or partner?
What are your charges, and how will you be paid for the advice?

faqs.q: Can an adviser near me get me a better annuity rate than my pension provider?
faqs.a: Annuity rates differ between providers, so comparing quotes across the market is a normal step. An adviser can shop around on your behalf rather than you accepting the first offer from your existing provider.
An enhanced annuity pays a higher income if you have certain health conditions or lifestyle factors that may shorten your life expectancy. An adviser can help you work out whether you might qualify.

faqs.q: Do I have to buy an annuity with my whole pension pot?
faqs.a: No, you can usually use part of your pot to buy an annuity and keep the rest invested or take it another way. An adviser can explain the options for your particular pension.

faqs.q: How do I check that an annuity adviser is properly authorised?
faqs.a: Look up the adviser or firm on the FCA register to confirm they are authorised or an appointed representative of an authorised firm. If something goes wrong you can complain to the firm, then to the Financial Ombudsman Service.

extra_heading: What happens when you first speak to an annuity adviser
extra: A first conversation with an annuity adviser is mostly about your circumstances rather than products. They will want to know how your pension is held, roughly what it is worth, when you want income to start, and whether anyone else depends on that income. Expect questions about your health and lifestyle too, because these can shape whether an enhanced annuity is worth exploring.

From there the adviser can explain how a single life annuity differs from one that continues for a spouse or partner, and what inflation protection would mean for the income you start with. They may show you illustrations based on different choices so you can see the trade-offs rather than deciding in the abstract. Nothing should be rushed, and you are free to go away and think.

If you are over fifty and have a defined contribution pension, Pension Wise offers free, impartial guidance that can help you understand your options before you speak to an adviser. That guidance is not a personal recommendation, so it works well alongside regulated advice rather than instead of it.

extra_faqs.q: Is an annuity adviser the same as a pension adviser?
extra_faqs.a: Annuity advice is a specialism within pension advice, so many pension advisers also deal with annuities. When you enquire, say clearly that you are considering an annuity so we introduce you to someone who works in that area.

extra_faqs.q: Can I speak to an adviser before I have decided anything?
extra_faqs.a: Yes, and it is often sensible to do so early. An adviser can set out how annuities compare with other ways of taking your pension, so you are deciding with a clear picture rather than after you have already committed.

extra_faqs.q: What if I only want a small annuity?
extra_faqs.a: You can usually use part of your pension pot to buy an annuity and leave the rest as it is. Tell the adviser how much of your pot you want to use so the advice matches what you actually intend to do.
